title: What If You Never Slept Again?

scenes.narration: What if, starting tonight, you never slept again? No naps, no nights, just one endless day.
Tap like if you're watching this way past bedtime.
After seventeen to nineteen hours awake, people in one study did as badly on tests as someone with a blood alcohol level of point zero five percent.
In a famous 1964 experiment, a seventeen-year-old student stayed awake for eleven days, about two hundred sixty-four hours.
Part of the reason we can't skip it: in mice, sleep widens the space between brain cells by about sixty percent, so fluid can flush out waste.
Scientists think sleep may be, in part, a nightly cleaning shift for the brain.
Even animals that can't stop still sleep. Frigatebirds flying for days over the ocean nap mid-flight, sometimes with just half their brain.
About forty-two minutes of sleep a day in the air, compared with roughly twelve hours on land.
So evolution never deleted sleep. It just found ways to do it with half a brain.

claims.claim: After 17-19 hours without sleep, test performance was equivalent to or worse than at 0.05% BAC
In 1963-64 a 17-year-old stayed awake about 11 days (264 hours)
In mice, sleep increased the brain's interstitial space by about 60%, increasing clearance of waste such as beta-amyloid
Researchers suggest the brain may flush out toxins during sleep
Great frigatebirds sleep in flight, sometimes with one hemisphere at a time
Frigatebirds slept about 42 minutes a day in flight versus about 12 hours a day on land
